newsitem.title: USA: Amerin says HUD issues opinion on captives.
newsitem.headline: Amerin says HUD issues opinion on captives.

text.p: Amerin Guaranty Corp, a mortgage insurance company, said Monday the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development has issued a formal opinion stating that captive reinsurance arrangements are permissible under a federal consumer protection law.

Captive reinsurance is a relatively new insurance product pioneered by Amerin, the company said. Under the arrangements, banks set up reinsurance companies with mortgage insurers such as Amerin. In exchange for sharing a certain amount of risk on loans, banks receive a portion of premium revenue from Amerin.

The company said it sought the opinion from HUD because the department oversees the Real Estate Settlement Act, which is a law designed to protect consumers in real estate transactions. In January, the U.S. Treasury Department's comptroller of currency approved the first captive deal.

"Amerin has designed captives that are conservatively structured, adequately capitalized and provide real risk transference. HUD's opinion reaffirms our approach and lays out a roadmap to design legally compliant and financially sound captive arrangements," Amerin chairman and chief executive gerald Friedman said in a statement.
